sections.h2: Which Lawrenceburg offices touch an Anderson County tax bill?
sections.html:
Two do. The Sheriff, in the building at 208 S Main St, collects the money and answers questions at (502) 839-4021 on weekdays between seven in the morning and five in the afternoon. The Property Valuation Administrator, at (502) 839-4061, owns the number that the bill is built on. Lawrenceburg is the only city in a county of roughly 202 square miles, so crossroads places such as Alton and McBrayer deal with the same pair of offices.

The Sheriff mails bills in the last days of September and starts collecting on October 1. Mortgage companies no longer receive copies, which means a borrower whose lender pays out of escrow should phone the servicer in October and ask whether the bill reached it.

sections.h2: How fast does an unpaid Anderson County bill grow?
sections.html:
The county follows the state calendar in KRS 134.015 and posts it on the Sheriff's page. Cash, checks and money orders are accepted. Part payments are turned away, and a postmark earns nothing, since the money must land in the office on the date.

What the Anderson County Sheriff does with a bill, stage by stage
StageDatesEffect on the amount
EarlyOctober 1 to November 1Two percent comes off
PlainNovember 2 to December 31The printed amount
First penaltyJanuary 1 to 31Five percent on top
Second penaltyFebruary 1 until the office shuts on April 15Ten percent, plus ten percent more as the Sheriff's fee

After that last day the bill is no longer the Sheriff's problem. It becomes a certificate of delinquency at the County Clerk, with a 20 percent County Attorney charge, a 10 percent Clerk charge and monthly interest of 1 percent layered on. The Sheriff's page adds that the debt can be sold to an outside buyer in summer.

sections.h2: What does the state's own example show?
sections.html:
Kentucky's revenue agency walks a $1,000 bill through the process. With the 10 percent penalty, the Sheriff's add-on and an assumed 4 percent commission, it arrives at the clerk as $1,254. Cleared within five business days the example comes to $1,387.79, and after the county attorney's first letter it is $1,611.30. Commission rates differ by county, so Anderson County owners should treat these as a rough scale and ask the clerk for a real payoff.

  • First letter from the county attorney: within 30 days of the transfer.
  • Sale: at least 90 and at most 135 days after the transfer, under KRS 134.128.
  • Notice: a newspaper advertisement and a posting on a county website.

sections.h2: Is it worth contesting a valuation in Anderson County?
sections.html:
If a figure looks high, the road is narrow but clear. Values are set as of January 1. The roll is shown to the public for 13 days from the first Monday in May. Before anything can be filed you must sit down with the PVA or a deputy. Then you have until the close of the next business day after the roll closes to file at the County Clerk's office.

The local board of assessment appeals, in session up to five days starting 25 to 35 days after the roll closes, hears the case. Bring written proof: land and building descriptions, insurance policies, what the building cost, and sales listings. A filing with nothing attached fails. A person who does not appear at the board loses the right to carry the case further, and a higher final value than you claimed produces an extra bill for the gap.

sections.h2: Does an Anderson County senior pay less?
sections.html:
An owner aged 65 or more, or one classified as totally disabled, can claim a Kentucky homestead exemption by applying to the PVA. The Sheriff's tax page points those owners to the PVA line. The deduction is $49,100 from the assessed value for 2025 and 2026, a figure the state resets every second year. On a house assessed at $200,000, the state's own example, tax is figured on $150,900.

A birth certificate, driver's license or passport proves age. Disability claims need annual renewal, with exceptions for service-connected disabled veterans and anyone found permanently and totally disabled by Social Security or Kentucky Retirement Systems.

sections.h2: How has Anderson County changed, and why does it matter at tax time?
sections.html:
Anderson County had 14,571 people in 1990 and 23,852 in 2020, and the Census Bureau's mid-2025 estimate is 25,225. Wikipedia ranks it the ninth fastest-growing county in Kentucky. Growth shows up in houses: 10,652 housing units in July 2025, and 147 building permits issued that year. The 2020 count put the median age at 42.0 and found 56.8 percent of residents in urban areas.

  • Typical value of an owner-occupied home, 2020 to 2024: $225,100.
  • Households that own: 77.6 percent of 9,653.
  • Midpoint household income: $74,488; midpoint gross rent: $927.
  • Typical owner costs: $1,391 a month with a mortgage, $411 without.

An owner who bought in the previous year can list the deed price as the value for the next January 1 if nothing about the property has changed. In a county that has added so many homes, comparing your bill with neighbors' recent sales is a sensible first step before the roll opens.

sections.h2: What should a seller with back taxes do?
sections.html:
• Ask the Sheriff for the current bill and any older balance, or the Clerk once April 15 has gone by.
  • Tell the closing agent to pay arrears out of your proceeds and record the lien release.
  • Write the buyer's mailing address into the deed, since KRS 382.135 requires an in-care-of address for the tax bill.
  • If you hold a homestead exemption, ask the PVA how the sale affects it.

An owner who is behind and would rather skip repairs can ask for a written cash offer. The buyer's closing agent deducts taxes and clerk charges from the price, the way any closing does.

faqs.q: When does the early-payment discount end?
faqs.a: On November 1. KRS 134.015 gives 2 percent off to a taxpayer who pays in full by then, and the printed amount is owed through December 31.

faqs.q: What do I owe if I pay in February?
faqs.a: The printed amount plus 10 percent as a penalty and another 10 percent as the Sheriff's fee, according to the Sheriff's schedule for February 1 through April 15.

faqs.q: Can I pay half now and half later?
faqs.a: No. The Sheriff's Office does not take partial payments. A check postmarked in time but received late is treated as late.

faqs.q: Where do I start if my assessment seems too high?
faqs.a: With a conference at the PVA's office. A filing at the County Clerk cannot go forward without one, and the deadline falls the next business day after the roll closes.

faqs.q: How much does the homestead exemption take off?
faqs.a: The exemption is $49,100 off the assessed value for the 2025 and 2026 years. The PVA takes applications from owners who are 65 or older or totally disabled.
